newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ex-BoF member sees more German rate cuts-Le Monde.
newsitem.headline: Ex-BoF member sees more German rate cuts-Le Monde.

text.p: Former Bank of France Monetary Policy Council member Jean Boissonnat said he believed Germany would cut interest rates again, according to an interview published on Monday in French daily Le Monde.

Boissonnat also said in the interview he was convinced French and German interest rates would converge, but the idea that France should lower rates below Germany's simply to blow its own trumpet was childish.
Boissonnat said, "First, bearing in mind the German economic situation, I don't believe the easing cycle in Frankfurt has come to an end.

"Following that, I'm convinced that the natural progression for French and German rates is convergence, but there is no reason why the rates of one be permanently lower than those of the other," he said in the interview.
"The idea that France would have to lower its rates below those of the Bundesbank, simply to blow its own trumpet, seems to me like a childish attitude."
Boissonnat left the nine-member Bank of France monetary policy council earlier this year.
